title: What If the Laki Eruption Happened Again?

scenes.text: What if Iceland's Laki volcano erupted again? Most of the damage came from the air.
In 1783, a fissure about twenty-five kilometers long, with at least a hundred thirty vents, erupted for eight months.
It released about a hundred twenty million tonnes of sulfur dioxide, roughly six times the Pinatubo eruption.
In Iceland, around eighty percent of the sheep died, and about a fifth of the people died from famine and polluted air.
The haze spread across Europe within weeks. An estimated twenty thousand people died in Britain alone.
The summer was hot and the winter brutal. The deadliest part of this eruption was a gas you can't see.

description:
What if Iceland's Laki volcano erupted again?
In 1783 it poured out about 120 million tonnes of sulfur dioxide, killed a fifth of Iceland and an estimated 20,000 people in Britain.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: A volcano killed more people with gas than with lava. Which disaster should we run through next?
